newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas rallies late, June hits 14-week high.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas rallies late, June hits 14-week high.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures continued to rally late Thursday in fairly active trade, with technical buying adding fuel to the move when June broke to a new 14-week high by early afternoon, sources said.
At 1400 EDT, May was still up 6.1 cents at $2.245 per million British thermal units after rallying to $2.28. June was 5.1 cents higher at $2.255. Others also were up.

"There seems to be a tighter balance between supply and demand, and technically, there's no producer (sell) paper. No one wants to sell it, but I don't think you can justify prices in the $2.30s this early in the season," a Midwest trader said.

Most agreed early news Houston Light's 1,250 megawatt South Texas 1 nuclear unit shut unexpectedly got the bulls running. The company later said the unit would begin restart Friday and reach full power Saturday.
But traders said hotter weather next week in Texas and the West coupled with steady storage buying and possible heating loads in the upper Midwest may be enough to underpin physical prices near-term.
Chart traders said the market may be overbought and due for a correction after a three-day rally of almost 20 cents with sharp gains in open interest.
"Technically, it's still supportive, but it might be a little overbought in the short-term. I can't see putting on new length at these levels," a Texas trader said.
Traders said June's break today of resistance at $2.24 could set up a test of the $2.385 contract high. Support was seen at $2.05 and then along the up trendline at $2.01.
In the cash, Gulf Coast swing prices firmed a couple of cents to the mid-teens. Midcon pipes were up about a nickel to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas also gained five cents to the mid-$2.40s.
NYMEX said 26,666 contracts traded at 1300 EDT.
On the KCBT, June firmed 7.3 cents to $2.09, while deferreds were steady to six cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.2 cents to 15.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
